MINUTES
  MALIBU PLANNING COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  DECEMBER 5, 2022
  TELECONFERENCED VARIOUS LOCATIONS
  -

  6:30 P.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Orders N-25-20 and N-29-
20 and fully teleconferenced from various locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19)
pandemic.

CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Smith called the meeting to order at 6:32 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Dennis R. Smith, Vice Chair John Mazza and Commissioners Kraig Hill,
  Jeffrey Jennings and Mark Wetton

  ALSO PRESENT: Trevor Rusin, Interim City Attorney; Richard Mollica, Planning
  Director; Yolanda Bundy, City Building Official; Adrian Fernandez, Assistant Planning
  Director; Patricia Salazar, Development and Operations Manager; Raneika Brooks, Senior
  Planner; Tyler Eaton, Senior Planner; Lauren Doyel, Contract Coastal Engineer and
  Geotechnical Reviewer; Robert Ross, City Wireless Consultant; and Rebecca Evans,
  Recording Secretary

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Vice Chair Mazza moved and Commissioner Wetton seconded a motion to approve
  the agenda as recommended by staff and to continue Item Nos. 4.B. and 5.B. to a
  date uncertain.

  The question was called and the motion carried unanimously.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Recording Secretary Evans reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted
  on November 23, 2022. The amended agenda was properly posted on December 1, 2022.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS
  None.

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS
  None.

ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION / STAFF COMMENTS

  Vice Chair Mazza suggested the Planning Commission consider an earlier cutoff
  point for supplemental agenda reports. He suggested an additional fee for design
  changes requested after a project has been deemed complete might help alleviate
  the current backlog. He noted new Planning Commissioners would benefit from a
  training session before facing a demanding schedule. Vice Chair Mazza expressed
  his thanks for the service of Commissioners Jennings and Wetton.

  Commissioner Hill agreed that an earlier cutoff date for supplemental reports may
  be helpful. He requested staff updates on the status of the Hosted Short-Term Rental
  Ordinance discussions with California Coastal Commission, the Mountains
  Recreation and Conservation Authority request for California Department of
  Transportation funding for lateral ocean access points, Accessory Dwelling Unit
  Ordinance reports requested by the Planning Commission, additional trails planned
  in Malibu and he requested future California Department of Transportation Pacific
  Coast Highway projects include traffic flow reports. Commissioner Hill thanked
  Commissioner Jennings for his years of service to the City of Malibu and for his
  strict but fair treatment of the issues. Commissioner Hill noted California Coastal
  Commission planned a hearing on a secant wall and the Mountains Recreation and
  Conservation Authority asked for a condition of approval to fund a lateral ocean
  access point where there is little or no dry beach. He questioned the nexus for
  highway repair and funding for coastal access.

  Commissioner Jennings read an article about the Riddick decision and would like
  some feedback on an ongoing basis from staff on potential impacts for how the
  Commissioners should appropriately handle similar hearings based on the trial
  court findings. The Los Angeles Times indicated City Council decided to take the
  case on appeal, which he found surprising because trial cases do not set precedent.
  He thanked Commissioners Mazza and Hill for their kind words.

  Commissioner Wetton thanked the Commission and expressed appreciation for
  City staff. He expressed interest in serving with the Commission at some point in
  the future. He requested an update from staff on the Accessory Dwelling Unit
  Ordinance.
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes of December 5, 2022
  Page 3 ofl2

 Vice Chair Mazza informed a startup, Samara, will mass produce studio and one-
 bedroom units and was founded by a co-founder of Airbnb. He stated the Accessory
 Dwelling Unit and Short-Term Rental conversations were linked.

 Chair Smith thanked Commissioner Jennings and noted it was an honor to serve on
 the Planning Commission with him. He thanked Commissioner Wetton for his
 service.

Planning Director Mollica expressed understanding regarding concerns about the
72-hour requirement for supplemental agenda reports and noted the department
would continue to endeavor to hold to the typical schedule. However, the
Thanksgiving holiday created challenges for the December 5, 2022 agenda packet.
He confirmed that training had historically been provided for new Commissioners
and in the past training was provided in-person by the League of Cities but moved
to a virtual format during COVID- 19.

Interim Assistant Attorney Rusin confirmed that procedural manuals and Brown
Act training sessions would be provided to new Commissioners and available as a
refresher for experienced Commissioners who were interested in participating.
In response to Vice Chair Mazza, Planning Director Mollica noted that the City had
a revision fee and he would review its application.

Planning Director Mollica stated the California Coastal Commission heard the City
of Malibu’s Short-Term Rental Local Coastal Program Amendment in August and
did not approve it. The Department planned to bring an item to the City Council in
January to request direction. The California Coastal Commission offered to work
with the City to clarify their concerns and propose changes. The City Council would
be asked if they prefer Planning negotiate with California Coastal Commission or
pursue a set direction.

In response to Commissioners Hill and Wetton, Planning Director Mollica stated
the Planning Commission’s list of additional requests for consideration of the
Accessory Dwelling Ordinance was taken to City Council and the Council directed
staff to prepare an Ordinance which closely mirrored the current second unit
regulations in Malibu’s Local Coastal Program. The item would likely be heard in
February 2023 and if the pleasure of the Planning Commission, could be heard in a
special meeting or as part of a regular meeting.

In response to Commissioner Jennings, Interim City Attorney Rusin stated the City
was not asked for comment on the recent Riddick case article and the article
contained many inaccuracies. The trial court decision conflicted with both the City
interpretation and guidance of the California Coastal Commission and the case had
been appealed by the City. (7 PM);
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes of December 5, 2022
  Page4ofl2

Planning Director Mollica informed that Contract Planner Smith created a trails
map for the trails incentive program the City Council considered. The map was
submitted to the California Coastal Commission and their requested changes, which
included the addition of a trail, raised substantial concern. The City Council voted
to deny certification and the matter was then removed from staffs work plan.

 The Mountains Recreation and Conservation Authority had a public works plan
 pending for the last decade to address public access which included vertical access
 and campgrounds within the City of Malibu. The plan had never been finalized but
 as part of the plan, there was a proposed accessway approximately 1,000 feet to the
 east of the proposed secant wall. While the secant wall lies within the City’s
jurisdiction, the toe of that lies within State lands and the California Coastal
Commission did not allow the City to take up that part of the plan. As part of their
approval, the California Coastal Commission proposed a special condition, which
required the California Department of Transportation fund part of the draft public
works plan. This condition included a stairwell at Las Tunas. The City would send
a comment letter to California Coastal Commission and express that the Mountains
Recreation and Conservation Authority should bring a Coastal Development Permit
application to the City.

Interim City Attorney Rusin expressed strong concerns about nexus and
proportionality in the California Coastal Commission proposal. However, the
application is from the California Department of Transportation so the City would
not have control.

In response to Interim City Attorney Rusin, Vice Chair Mazza asked if the prior
court case against Edmonson regarding a Public Works Plan at Bluffs Park would
apply to the situation.

Interim City Attorney Rusin noted the item was somewhat different and was not
agendized so discussion would be minimal. He expressed thanks to all of the
Commissioners for the time devoted to Planning Commission work.

Planning Director Mollica thanked the Commissioners for their work throughout
the year and wished them a happy holiday.

Chair Smith and Planning Director Mollica congratulated Tyler Eaton on his
promotion to Senior Planner. Senior Planner Eaton began his career as a Planning
Department Intern and had shown tremendous professional growth during his years
with Malibu.

Senior Planner Eaton expressed his thanks to the Commissioners for their
contributions to his growth as a planner.
